To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we develop methods for estimating the number of fish with a particular health status, H, from a known total number N of fish in a pond, when the health status is determined by a capture-recapture process that is based on information from two qualitatively different sources, and we show that the estimates are unbiased if the probability of being captured by the net, given health status and being captured by the rod, satisfies certain assumptions.
we have developed methods for a capture-recapture problem in which information comes from two qualitatively different sources, one of which does not provide information about the absence of disease.
we have developed three methods for estimating the number of fish that are healthy when they are first tagged.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of capture-recapture methods when information comes from two qualitatively different sources.
estimating the total number of fish in a population, where the fish are healthy at the time of tagging, but may become sick later.
the estimation of a population parameter, the total number of individuals with a particular characteristic, when the population is not directly accessible.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, under assumptions that are reasonable in the WTC setting, the method proposed here is a useful tool in the follow-up of WTC responders, and that, in the absence of other information, the method should be used.
the methods developed for the fish problem can be applied to the follow-up problem.
the three estimates of H are asymptotically unbiased and that they bracket H under the stated assumptions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the methods we have developed can be used to obtain estimates of the total number of healthy fish in a population, and can be used to estimate the number with disease in a group of responders to a clean-up site.
the capture-recapture methods developed are useful when information is obtained from two qualitatively different sources.
the three estimates are all consistent, but that the middle one has the lowest mean squared error.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of missingness and nonresponse, one should use multiple data sources to estimate the number with a particular characteristic of interest.
the capture-recapture problem can be solved by a method that is qualitatively different from those in the standard literature.
the capture-recapture problem is more complicated than previously recognized.
